missions.title: The Crooked Margin
missions.knowledgeQuestion: Who checks what gets lost when a warning has to fit?

objectives.title: Pull both press proofs and find the signed ramp order.
Get the ramp instructions to the landing, or hand them back to Lark.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: That short guide is for runners’ pockets. The order is already in the type bed. Pull one sheet and leave the type where it is.

options.text: Slide in a short sheet and pull the lever.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: The proof says WEST RAMP OPEN. The small type stops at the edge. If you’re a cart with no load and very small handwriting, it’s a splendid notice.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: Use the same type bed with the full-width guide. The wide sheet takes longer to hang because it has to be tied in two places.

options.text: Slide in a full sheet and pull the lever.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: WEST RAMP OPEN — EMPTY CARTS, THIS SHIFT ONLY. The hoist directions and the signature fit beneath. Same ink, same type, different edge. Put both proofs against the signed order at the landing.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: The trial was with an empty cart. I can send a whole sheet to the ramp queue, but runners can’t carry it to the stalls yet. Or I can cut a separate strip, stamp it to match the turn arrow, and ask a runner to hang them together.

options.text: Fold the full order for the ramp queue.
Clip a turn arrow to its matching strip for the runner.
Hand back the proofs. Let the crew give directions until the next checked print.
Leave the tray here for now.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: There’s a cord at the far end of the landing. Pull the lower fold through it so people can read the hoist line while they wait.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: The runner is using two hooks near the press passage. Set the arrow beside the matching strip before she sets off. A person seeing only the arrow will miss who it’s for.

dialogue.speaker: copies-presskeeper
dialogue.text: I’ll mark that as held. Someone has to leave the loading crew and call the turns until there’s a sheet they’ll sign for.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A carter with a full load holds the back of the sheet flat against the board. From here, you can see their crew’s hoist beyond the steps.

options.text: Tie the lower fold open so the queue can see both routes.
Keep the sheet folded for now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The carter lifts a hand to the hoist crew and leaves the ramp queue. At the outer stalls, people ask when their runner will arrive. Lark sends a sample fold to the Council.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The runner clips a bag shut. She can reach the stalls before they load their carts. There’s room on the two hooks for the arrow and its matching limit.

options.text: Hang the arrow and trial strip side by side.
Ask the runner to wait a little.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A stall keeper sends the loaded carts to the hoist before they join the ramp queue. The runner stops to re-clip a loose strip. Lark sends a sample pair to the Council.

hints.text: Lark can use the same type with more than one kind of paper.
Both guides are near the landing passage in the Print Workshop.
Pull a proof on each guide without changing the type.
Read the signed ramp order at the far end of the Lending Hall Landing, above the runner’s landing copy.
Lark will work with either way of carrying the warning.
Use the tray next to the guides, just before the press passage to the landing.
The full order goes to the far ramp. A paired order goes on the runner’s hooks on the near side.
Tie the wide order open, hang the matched pair, or hand back the proofs at the tray and leave the crew to call turns.

journal.text: The narrow guide left a route arrow and cut off the crew’s trial limit. A wider guide caught both. Lark and the landing crew weighed where the warning would reach people and how it would stay together.
